_comment: Hindu expansion 175-drive G: Mahabharata war-catalysis episodes (Ganguli 1883-96, public domain).

region.zh: 陀夷多湖，林居（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Vana Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Vana Parva, Yaksha Prashna

summary.en: A crane at a forest lake killed four brothers who drank without answering its riddle. Yudhishthira came last, gave the answers - 'the greatest wonder is that men die every day, and the living walk on as if immortal' - and was offered one brother's life. He chose Nakula, his stepmother's son: justice over blood, and the crane was Dharma, his father, giving him back all five.
summary.zh: 林中湖畔的怪鳥誅殺了四個未答其謎即飲水的兄弟。堅戰最後到來，給出答案——『最大的奇蹟是人們日日赴死，而生者仍如不死般行走』——並被允許救活一位兄弟。他選擇繼母之子無種：公道勝過血緣；而怪鳥即是正法，其父，歸還五子。

passages.text: One by one the four Pandavas drank at the unseen lake and were struck down by its voice: this water is guarded; answer before you drink. Only their brother was left to come looking. Yudhishthira answered every question - what is the greatest marvel? Men die daily, and the living walk as if immortal; what is the best wealth? Knowledge; what is the greatest gain? Health; what is dharma? The conduct of the good.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The reward offered was one brother; he chose Nakula, Madri's son, so that both his mothers would have a survivor - and the crane stood up as Dharma, the god of justice, his own father, restored all four: the ethics exam passed by the only student it was set for.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: The Dice Game in the Hall of Kauravas

texts.period: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Sabha Parva, the game of dice

summary.en: Summoned by a friendly invitation that was a trap, Yudhishthira sat down to dice against Shakuni, who played with his brother's charred bones - dice that obeyed him. Kingdom, brothers, self, Draupadi: all staked and lost in an afternoon. Her question in the assembly - 'whom have you lost first, yourself or me?' - broke the hall's law open; what followed made the war.
summary.zh: 以友善之名實為陷阱的邀請召堅戰入局，對手沙恭尼執其兄之焦骨所製之骰——骰子聽其號令。王國、兄弟、自身、黑公主：一個下午盡數押上並輸掉。她在集會上的質問——『你先輸的是你自己還是我？』——撕裂了廷堂之法；隨後之事釀成大戰。

passages.text: Shakuni's dice were made from the bones of his own ruined family and obeyed him like servants; against them Yudhishthira, incapable of refusing a challenge, staked the kingdom as he had been taught dharma - by losing it. Brother by brother, self by self, he staked and lost - and when nothing was left, Dushasana was sent to drag Draupadi, dressed for menstruation, into the hall of men as the last stake won.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Sabha Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Her question to the assembly - was I lost before or after you lost yourself? - hung over the elders who kept their eyes down; the attempt to disrobe her was answered by the sari that would not end, and Bhima's vow that day put the war on its calendar.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Sabha Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.zh: 克里希那最後一次赴象城

texts.period: Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Udyoga Parva, Krishna's peace mission

summary.en: Before the war, Krishna went unarmed to Duryodhana's court to ask for five villages - anything, he said, rather than the blood of two houses. Duryodhana offered not a pin's point of land. Krishna's answer was the cosmic form shown to the court, the sanction of the war, and the choice given to each side - and the age chose.
summary.zh: 戰前，克里希那空手赴難敵之廷，求取五村——他說，兩族之血，任何代價都勝過。難敵連一根針尖之地也不予。克里希那的回答是向王廷顯示宇宙之形、戰爭之許可，以及給予雙方的選擇——而這個時代做出了選擇。

passages.text: Krishna's offer was a masterpiece of smallness: five villages for five princes - a grain of the contested earth - so that no one could say war was chosen over land. Duryodhana refused even the pin's point, and ordered the envoy seized; Krishna rose from his seat, unfolded his cosmic form before the court, and the age saw what it was electing.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The embassy's record stands in the epic as the last moral exit: the war was not forced by land-grab but by a court that would not grant a village's worth of peace - the doctrine that choices, not fates, made Kurukshetra.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

region.zh: 喜馬拉雅仙居（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi/Vana Parva traditions, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), the curses of Karna

summary.en: Rejected by every teacher because of his charioteer birth, Karna learned from the sage Parashurama by pretending to be a brahmin. A nap in the teacher's lap ended the disguise: a bee's sting drew blood, the master woke to see a kshatriya's endurance, and the curse fell - the weapon you learned shall fail you when you need it. A cow's curse and a beggar's curse stacked the same verdict: the finest archer of the age was scheduled to die by accident of timing.
summary.zh: 因御者之子之出身被所有教師拒絕，迦爾納偽裝婆羅門從仙人婆羅沙羅學藝。在教師膝上午睡斷送了偽裝：一隻蜂螫出血，師醒見其剎帝利之忍耐，詛咒遂降——你所學的武器將在你最需要時背棄你。母牛之詛咒與乞者之詛咒疊出同一判決：當世最優的射手，被預定死於時機的偶然。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; caste readings contested; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Parashurama taught only brahmins; Karna wore the sacred thread of a brahmin's son and learned the Brahmastra and the bow of heaven - the century's best student under a false name. The bee found his shoulder in the teacher's lap; he bore the sting in silence rather than wake his sleeping master, and the blood woke him instead: a kshatriya's silence is not a brahmin's patience - the weapon shall fail thee at the hour of thy death.

The second curse came from a brahmin whose cow Karna had accidentally killed in practice - thy wheel shall sink in the earth at the last. Both curses kept their word at Kurukshetra: the weapon forgotten in the mouth, the wheel swallowed by the field - a life's talent bankrupted by a life's small sins.

title.en: The Death of Drona: A Lie Told for a War
title.zh: 德羅納之死：為戰爭而說的謊

texts.period: Mahabharata, Drona Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Drona Parva, the fall of Drona

summary.en: Drona's chakravyuha was eating the Pandava army until Krishna proposed the one weapon that could stop him: a lie. An elephant named Ashwatthama was killed - and 'Ashwatthama is dead' was cried across the field, true of the elephant, false of the son. Drona asked Yudhishthira, the man who never lied; his broken answer - 'it is true, but not the man' - was lost in Krishna's conch, and the teacher dropped his bow.
summary.zh: 德羅納的輪陣正吞食般度軍隊，直到克里希那提出唯一能阻止他的武器：謊言。一頭名為馬音的大象被殺——『馬音已死』的呼喊傳遍戰場，於象為真，於子為假。德羅納問那個從不說謊的堅戰；他破碎的回答——『是，但不是那個人』——被克里希那的法螺聲吞沒，教師垂下了弓。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; the ethics of the lie are debated in the tradition itself; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The plan was honest about being dishonest: kill the elephant named Ashwatthama, then say the name - the teacher will ask only the man he trusts, and the man he trusts has never lied. Yudhishthira's answer tried to be both true and loyal: Ashwatthama is dead - the elephant, not the son - but the conch and the drums buried the second half of the sentence in the first half's sound.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Drona Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Drona, hearing his boy was gone, sat down on the field and closed his eyes in yoga; Dhrishtadyumna's sword did the rest - and the epic has argued ever since about the one sin that bought the war's turning point.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Drona Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Bhishma on the Bed of Arrows

texts.period: Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Bhishma Parva

summary.en: The grandfather of both armies was held up for ten days by his own vow - he could not be killed while he chose not to fall, and would not fight women or women-born. Shikhandin was brought against him; Arjuna's arrows passed behind that shield and stitched Bhishma to the earth. He lay on the arrows-bed for fifty-eight nights, teaching the dharma of kings while the war raged over him.
summary.zh: 兩軍共同的祖父被自己的誓言懸於十天之久——他不能在自己不願倒下時被殺，且不與女子或由女子所生者為戰。希甘丁被引至其前；阿周那之箭越過那道盾，把毗濕摩縫在地上。他在箭床上躺了五十八夜，一邊於戰火之中講授王法。

passages.text: Bhishma could not fall while he willed to stand: the boon of his father's blessing and the vow of his youth held him up while both armies battered; the age's finest archer was being killed by permission. The loophole was Shikhandin - the reborn Amba, whom he had wronged and could not fight; behind that shield Arjuna emptied his quiver, and the old man went down onto a bed of his own arrows.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: He chose the hour of his death: fifty-eight nights on the arrows, waiting for the sun's northern road, teaching Yudhishthira the duties of kings from a bed of pain - the epic's sage-parliament on the field it had helped to ruin.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

texts.period: Mahabharata, Drona Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Drona Parva, Abhimanyu episode

summary.en: Sixteen years old, Abhimanyu had heard in his mother's womb how to enter the Chakravyuha - but the exit lesson was interrupted. On the thirteenth day he broke into the wheel-formation alone, fought through its rings, and was killed in the closed center by six warriors breaking every rule of single combat. The boy's death broke the war's remaining decencies.
summary.zh: 十六歲的阿毗曼紐曾在母胎中聽聞入輪陣之法——但出口之課被打斷。第十三日，他獨自衝入車輪陣，連破其環，於封閉中心遭六名戰士違反單挑規則而圍殺。少年之死擊碎了戰爭僅存的體面。

passages.text: The lesson was interrupted at the exit: Arjuna's wife fell asleep as he explained the labyrinth of rings, and the boy in her womb learned the way in but not the way out - the epic's cruelest incomplete education. On the thirteenth day, with the formation spinning and his uncles pinned, Abhimanyu broke through the mouth of the wheel alone and cut his way ring by ring toward its center.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Drona Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Six warriors closed on one boy - wheel-hubs, swords, bows from every side; he died fighting with a wheel-broken bow, and the code of the field broke with him: the war had run out of rules it was willing to keep.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Drona Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

texts.period: Mahabharata, Shalya/Sauptika Parvas, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), the curse of Gandhari

summary.en: The blindfolded queen who had chosen her husband's darkness as her own walked through the field of her hundred dead sons and found Yudhishthira standing alive. Her grief opened - and her curse fell on Krishna: as thou hast watched my sons destroy each other, so shall thy house destroy itself, and the women of thy line shall weep as I do now. Thirty-six years later it came true.
summary.zh: 以布覆目、選擇與丈夫共享黑暗的王后，走過百子盡亡的戰場，發現堅戰仍活著。她的悲痛開口——詛咒降於克里希那：如你眼看我的兒子們互相毀滅，你的家也將自相殘殺，你家族的女子將如我今日般哭泣。三十六年後，此言應驗。

passages.text: Gandhari had worn the bandage since her wedding, sharing her blind husband's world; her hundred sons died in eighteen days - she came to the field led by hand, over the bodies of her house. Her foot found Yudhishthira alive where all her sons were not; the queen who had cursed no one cursed the god who had permitted it - the same grief, turned toward its author.

Krishna took the curse as his due: in the thirty-sixth year the Yadavas fell on each other on the beach at Prabhasa, and the women of Dvaraka wept on the shore - the epic's oldest rule, that every grief writes its own future.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Mausala Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.zh: 迦爾納陷於泥中的車輪

texts.period: Mahabharata, Karna Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Karna Parva

summary.en: On the seventeenth day, at the last duel of the age's two archers, the earth took Karna's chariot wheel - the curses of his teachers arriving on schedule. He asked Arjuna for the decency of the code: wait till I lift the wheel. Krishna reminded Arjuna of Draupadi and of every Karna courtesy refused - and the arrow flew while the wheel was being lifted.
summary.zh: 第十七日，當世兩位神射手的最後決鬥中，大地吞下迦爾納的戰車之輪——其師之詛咒如期而至。他請阿周那遵守戰場規矩：待我舉輪。克里希那向阿周那重提黑公主與迦爾納每一次被拒的禮數——而箭在車輪被抬起之時飛出。

passages.text: The wheel sank at the duel's hinge: two curses and a mother's missing gift stacked on one axle, and the sun-son stood half-buried asking for the code's mercy. Krishna's arithmetic was merciless: remember the dice-hall, remember the insults; the code was for men who kept it - and Arjuna's arrow was already loosed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Karna Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The epic refuses to close the case: Karna died cursing the god's fairness, and the age's finest generosity - his lifelong giving - was spent on a battlefield that took it for weakness; the war's moral ledger stays open on this page.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Karna Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Ashwatthama's Night Massacre and the Jeweled Forehead
title.zh: 馬音的夜襲與寶石之額

region.zh: 俱盧之野營地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Sauptika Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Sauptika Parva

summary.en: His father murdered by a lie, Ashwatthama entered the sleeping Pandava camp at night and killed everyone he could find, including the princes in their beds, and set the Khandava forest-fire of vengeance alight. Caught, he threw the Brahmashirsha at the womb of the last heir; Krishna cursed him to roam immortal - wound-ridden, begging from village to village, the gem on his brow the only evidence of what he was.
summary.zh: 其父死於謊言，馬音夜入沉睡的般度營，見人即殺，連床上王子亦不例外，並燃起復仇的乾達婆之火。被擒後，他將婆羅摩首箭射向最後繼承人的子宮；克里希那詛咒他永世漂泊——帶傷而行，沿村乞食，額上寶石成為他身份的唯一證據。

passages.text: The night raid avenged a father with a cemetery: the general's son swept the sleeping camp, killing princes in their beds and Draupadi's brothers in their tents - the war's last cruelty, done without a battle. His Brahmashirsha, aimed at Uttara's unborn son, was caught and turned by Krishna - the child was burned dark (hence Krishna, the dark one) and reborn as Parikshit, the survivor whose grandson would hear this very epic. The gem torn from his forehead was the price: immortal, festering, begging door to door for three ages - a walking sermon on what the war's last night cost the side that won it.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Sauptika Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
